intro.title: Write a function to merge objects deeply
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a JavaScript function that deeply merges two objects, combining their properties even when they are nested. You will learn the core programming concept of recursion, which allows a function to call itself to handle nested structures. The main technologies involved are JavaScript objects, conditional statements, and loops for iteration. By the end, you'll understand how to create a robust utility that can merge complex data structures, a common requirement in real-world applications.
intro.usecase: Deep object merging is essential when managing complex application state in real-world JavaScript applications. For example, when building dashboard interfaces that combine user preferences with default settings, developers need to merge configuration objects without losing nested properties. This pattern appears in form libraries that merge validation rules, e-commerce platforms that combine product variants, and content management systems that layer content overrides on base templates. Mastering deep merging helps developers handle configuration management, state updates, and data transformation tasks efficiently.
